item.title: Dictate 0.4.0
item.description:
Meetings

  • A second pillar next to dictation: drop a recorded meeting (far-field, several voices) into the window's Meetings section and get a speaker-labelled transcript, entirely on-device. You say how many people spoke; Whisper and speaker detection do the rest.
  • Read it your way: speaker turns on or off, talk time per speaker, long turns as paragraphs, rename Speaker A to a real name inline, tap any timestamp to hear that moment.
  • Search across every meeting with highlighted hits; export Markdown, plain text or SRT subtitles.
  • Summaries (Pro): with an AI provider configured — Apple Intelligence or any OpenAI-compatible server — a summary panel writes an overview, key points, action items and jump-to chapters on request. Hour-long meetings fit.
  • The setup sheet picks the meeting language (Auto, Russian, English) and the Whisper model per meeting, and shows the model's download size before you commit; the defaults live in Settings › Meetings.
  • Interrupted processing resumes where it stopped, a speaker-detection failure still delivers an unlabelled transcript, and "Reprocess" reruns a meeting through the current pipeline. Imports up to four hours long.
  • The meeting library is a resizable column of the window; ⌘1 / ⌘2 switch between Dictation and Meetings, ⌫ deletes the selected meeting, Space and ← / → drive playback in the transcript and the player.

Meeting recording (Pro)

  • Record the meeting in Dictate — the microphone, the system audio of a Zoom / Meet / Teams call, or both — from the Meetings section, the menu bar ("Record Meeting…") or a global shortcut.
  • The first recording that includes system audio asks once for System Audio Recording (Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording). Without it the recording contains silence, and Dictate says so after a few seconds instead of failing quietly.
  • A floating capsule shows the timer and levels and collapses to a pill; the menu-bar icon wears a recording badge. Dictation keeps working while a meeting records.
  • Recordings land in the library at once with a waveform player (scrub, ±15 s, 1×/1.5×/2×) and are transcribed when you ask.
  • Crash-safe: audio is written to disk as it happens. After a crash the recording comes back marked Recovered and is compacted to AAC in the background; quitting mid-recording asks first, and an app update that arrives mid-recording waits for the recording to stop before relaunching.
  • Four-hour meetings roll over into parts automatically. An hour costs about 15 MB (one source) or 30 MB (both) on disk.
  • Settings › Meetings: the record shortcut, default sources, permission status with a system-audio test, default language and Whisper model, speaker models (size, download, delete) and recording storage.
  • When a recording cannot start, the reason shows in a banner in the Meetings section; "Upgrade to Pro…" opens the License tab directly.

Dictation

  • No more phantom "Thank you." at the end of a dictation: the final decode no longer sees the room tone between your last word and the stop, and a segment that lies entirely over silence is dropped.
  • Buttons with a plain style now have a real hit target instead of only their label's pixels.

Knobs

  • defaults write com.f1lcry.localvoicer meetingPartSeconds -int N sets the length of one recording part before it rolls over.
